dct_description_sm: Abstract: This datalayer is a polygon coverage for Massachusetts displaying town boundaries and associated tabular data on substance abuse admissions (into licensed rehabilitation centers) per town per year. The date range covered here is from 1992-2001. The data here is derived from MassGIS (Town boundaries) and the BSAS Substance Abuse Treatment Fact Sheets on Statewide Admissions (attribute data). The Bureau of Substance Abuse Services (BSAS) is an agency of the Commonwealth of Massachusetts' Department of Public Health. This layer was derived from the Massachusetts Electronic Atlas database published by the Harvard Map Collection in 2001. The Massachusetts Electronic Atlas (MEA) was a collaborative project to provides access, via the Internet, to data about the Commonwealth, its thirteen regional planning agency districts and 351 cities and towns. This dataset is now only available via The Harvard Geospatial Library.

Purpose: This layer is intended for researchers, students, and policy makers for reference and mapping purposes, and may be used for basic applications such as viewing, querying, and map output production. This layer will provide a basemap for layers related to socio-political anaylsis, statistical enumeration and analysis, or to support graphical overlays and analysis with other spatial data. More advanced user applications may focus on demographics, urban and rural land use planning, socio-economic analysis and related areas including defining boundaries, managing assets and facilities, integrating attribute databases with geographic features, spatial analysis, and presentation output.

Supplemental information: The admissions rates and type of substance abuse are fully defined for the the first year of coverage included here (1992). Subsequent years simply follow the pattern of Total Admissions followed by the various types of substance abuse admissions which ocurred during that particular year.
